messages:
Jess (Sales): Hey team — Zenith POC hitting streaming failures. Browser client shows partial JSON objects and then SSE disconnects after ~30s. Can we triage?
Zenith-Eng: Confirmed. We see 'unexpected EOF' on the client and server logs show short writes. Happens behind our Cloudflare + nginx layer. Repro is consistent when responses exceed ~16k tokens.
Olivia (SRE): Thanks — @Jess are they on hosted Redwood API or Dedicated? Also what SDK/version and any proxy in front?
Jess (Sales): Hosted API (trial org). SDK v0.4.2 from their frontend. They have Cloudflare in front and an internal nginx reverse proxy. Logs attached below.
Zenith-Eng: Log snippet we captured:
```
2026-06-10T14:02:23Z INFO sse: wrote 204 bytes to client
2026-06-10T14:02:52Z WARN sse: client disconnected: read tcp 10.0.0.1:443->10.0.1.5:52344: unexpected EOF
2026-06-10T14:02:52Z INFO http: wrote 1 of 342 bytes
```
Mike (Eng): That looks a lot like intermediate buffering/truncation at the proxy. Many proxies will buffer until a buffer fills or until a newline; partial chunks can be dropped if connection is considered idle. Can you reproduce with curl -N? Example:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream"
```
If curl shows the same cut, the issue is upstream.
Olivia (SRE): Two quick fixes to try: 1) set X-Accel-Buffering: no on the nginx proxy or 2) set proxy_buffering off; in the nginx config. Also ensure Connection: keep-alive and Transfer-Encoding: chunked are preserved. Some CDNs strip those.
Mike (Eng): We can also add a temporary gateway header passthrough: if client sends `x-redwood-streaming: enable` we'll forward `X-Accel-Buffering: no` to the upstream. Doing that now as a short-term mitigation.
deploy-bot: config change applied to gateway (rev rwd-gw-2026-06-10-2) — forwarding X-Accel-Buffering for requests with x-redwood-streaming header.
Jess (Sales): Sent the SDK workaround to Zenith: set header `x-redwood-streaming: enable` and make sure their nginx has `proxy_buffering off;`. Also asked them to test with curl -N.
Zenith-Eng: Tried with the header and curl -N — stream stayed open and we saw the full JSON chunks. Looks much better. We're going to apply `proxy_buffering off;` in staging and test through Cloudflare.
Sam (CS): Great, do we need a permanent SDK change so customers get this header automatically?
Mike (Eng): Agree we should set the SDK to send x-redwood-streaming for streaming calls by default and document the nginx/CF settings. Also adding a note in the quickstart about `X-Accel-Buffering` and `Connection: keep-alive`.
Olivia (SRE): I'll follow up with an internal KB and an ops runbook for customers behind proxies/CDNs.
Jess (Sales): Thanks everyone — Zenith confirmed staging looks good. Marking this as resolved from sales side for now. :tada:
Zenith-Eng: Thanks team! We'll report back if Cloudflare layer needs additional config.
Mike (Eng): Leaving this open for a day to monitor, will close once no regressions. :thumbsup:
